package_info.package_manager: unknown (third-party eCommerce plugin, not a standard package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (attack leverages compromised or injected plugin, not a specific versioned package)
package_info.why_malicious: The QuickView plugin was compromised to inject a Magecart-style JavaScript skimmer into eCommerce sites. This malicious code dynamically loads a remote script from a lookalike domain, which harvests sensitive payment and credential data from users and exfiltrates it to an attacker-controlled server.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a user visits an affected eCommerce site
execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript via the QuickView third-party plugin or through a remote <script> tag in the site's HTML
required_permissions: Ability to create and append <script> elements
Read access to form fields (payment, credentials)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a user visits the compromised eCommerce site, the code dynamically creates and injects a <script> element that loads a remote JavaScript file from a malicious domain, enabling the remote script to access sensitive form fields and exfiltrate payment or credential data to an attacker-controlled server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code injects a remote script from an untrusted, lookalike domain, which is a hallmark of Magecart-style web skimming attacks. This allows attackers to execute arbitrary code in the user's browser and steal sensitive information.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate third-party scripts should only be loaded from well-known, verified domains and should not access or exfiltrate sensitive form data. Injecting scripts from domains that closely resemble trusted providers (e.g., gocgle-analytics.com instead of google-analytics.com) is highly abnormal and dangerous.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or payment providers may dynamically load scripts, but only from their official, verified domains and without accessing or exfiltrating sensitive user data.
key_indicators: Dynamic creation and injection of <script> elements referencing non-standard or lookalike domains
Obfuscated or base64-encoded JavaScript loaded at runtime
Access to sensitive form fields such as payment or login credentials by third-party scripts
Outbound network requests (e.g., POST) to attacker-controlled or recently registered domains with typosquatting characteristics

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises the QuickView third-party plugin or registers a lookalike domain (e.g., gocgle-analytics.com) to deliver malicious JavaScript.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious script is loaded onto eCommerce sites via the compromised plugin or injected <script> tag.

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is injected into the client-side environment when a user visits the affected eCommerce site.
attack_chain.leads_to: The injected script executes in the user's browser context.

attack_chain.action: The script reads sensitive data from payment or login forms present on the page.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collected data is prepared for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: The script exfiltrates the harvested data to an attacker-controlled remote domain using outbound network requests.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen credentials or payment information, achieving the final objective.

behavioral_signatures: Client-side JavaScript dynamically injecting <script> elements that load code from domains similar to trusted analytics or payment providers
Obfuscated or base64-encoded JavaScript loaded and executed at runtime
Third-party scripts accessing sensitive form fields (e.g., credit card numbers, login credentials) in the DOM
file_indicators: Injected <script> tags in HTML referencing non-standard or lookalike domains (e.g., gocgle-analytics.com)
Presence of dynamically created script elements in the DOM with suspicious src attributes
Obfuscated JavaScript code blocks present in plugin or site source files
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from client-side scripts to domains with typosquatting or recently registered domains (e.g., gocgle-analytics.com)
Unusual POST requests containing form data sent to unknown or untrusted remote servers
Network traffic to domains not present in the site's legitimate Content Security Policy (CSP)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor client-side script activity for dynamic script injection, especially from domains that closely resemble trusted providers. Use Content Security Policy (CSP) violation reports to detect unauthorized script sources. Analyze browser network traffic for outbound requests to suspicious or lookalike domains, and flag scripts that access sensitive form fields or use obfuscation techniques. Regularly audit third-party plugins and their loaded resources for unauthorized modifications or injections.
